title: GUIs Must Be Parented Correctly
summary: A Frame floating in Workspace or a random Folder will never render. ScreenGuis must live in PlayerGui/StarterGui; GuiObjects must be descendants of a ScreenGui (or SurfaceGui/BillboardGui).

explanation.whatItIs: The rendering contract: the GUI renderer only walks GUI containers. Anything parked elsewhere exists but is invisible.
explanation.whyItExists: Separating 3D content from 2D overlays lets the engine batch and clip UI efficiently.
symptoms: Frame created, parented to workspace — nothing appears
TextLabel exists (FindFirstChild works) yet stays invisible
explanation.fix: Chain: PlayerGui → ScreenGui → (frames/labels/buttons). Surface/Billboard GUIs parent to parts but follow the same 'inside a GUI container' rule.
tips: Build in Studio Explorer with correct parenting, then replicate the structure in code
Debug invisibility by walking ancestors: every hop must be GUI-ish
commonMistakes: Parenting ScreenGui to Workspace by accident
GuiObjects under Model/Folder 'for organization' inside PlayerGui — still invisible
SurfaceGui without a valid Adornee part

examples.title: Valid chains
examples.code:
-- ✅ Renders:
-- Players.You.PlayerGui.MenuScreen (ScreenGui).Title (TextLabel)

-- ❌ Invisible:
-- workspace.MenuScreen.Title
-- Players.You.PlayerGui.StuffFolder… wait, that one ALSO fails:
-- PlayerGui → Folder → Frame   ✘ (Folder is not a GUI container)

local playerGui = game.Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = playerGui          -- GUI container ✔

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Parent = screen              -- directly under ScreenGui ✔
label.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 50)
